⌄ Classifier Comparison on the Loan Approval Dataset

Naive Bayes vs. SVM vs. Decision Tree (CART) vs. MLP

This notebook evaluates four classic classification algorithms with different hyperparameter configurations on the historical Loan Approval Dataset.

Dataset used: Loan Eligibility Prediction Dataset (Historical retail banking records across 614 applicant credit profiles).

Algorithms compared:

  • Gaussian Naive Bayes — default variance smoothing and custom smoothing configurations.
  • Support Vector Machine (SVM) — Linear and RBF non-linear kernels across regularization values.
  • Decision Tree — CART — Gini impurity vs Entropy splits with depth constraints.
  • Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) — Deep feed-forward neural networks with ReLU and Tanh activations.

⌄ 3. Preprocessing
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline # 1. Separate features and target X_raw = df.drop(['Loan_ID', TARGET_COL], axis=1) y_raw = df[TARGET_COL].map({'Y': 1, 'N': 0}) # 2. Impute and One-Hot Encode num_cols = X_raw.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns cat_cols = X_raw.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns preprocessor = ColumnTransformer([ ('num', Pipeline([('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')), ('scaler', StandardScaler())]), num_cols), ('cat', Pipeline([('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')), ('onehot', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False))]), cat_cols) ]) # 3. Train-test split (80/20 stratified) X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_raw, y_raw, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_raw) X_train_s = preprocessor.fit_transform(X_train) X_test_s = preprocessor.transform(X_test) print("Train shape:", X_train_s.shape, " Test shape:", X_test_s.shape)
Train shape: (491, 20) Test shape: (123, 20)
⌄ 4. Helper: train + evaluate any model

One function handles training, prediction, metrics, confusion matrix, and ROC-AUC scoring across all algorithms.

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score, confusion_matrix, roc_auc_score, roc_curve, log_loss import time results = [] roc_data = {} trained_models = {} def evaluate_model(name, model, X_tr, y_tr, X_te, y_te): start = time.time() model.fit(X_tr, y_tr) train_time = time.time() - start y_pred = model.predict(X_te) metrics = { "Model": name, "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y_te, y_pred), "Precision": precision_score(y_te, y_pred, average="weighted", zero_division=0), "Recall": recall_score(y_te, y_pred, average="weighted", zero_division=0), "F1": f1_score(y_te, y_pred, average="weighted", zero_division=0), "Train time (s)": round(train_time, 4) } if hasattr(model, "predict_proba"): proba = model.predict_proba(X_te) metrics["Log Loss"] = log_loss(y_te, proba) metrics["ROC-AUC"] = roc_auc_score(y_te, proba[:, 1]) fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_te, proba[:, 1]) roc_data[name] = (fpr, tpr, metrics["ROC-AUC"]) cm = confusion_matrix(y_te, y_pred) results.append(metrics) trained_models[name] = model return metrics, cm
⌄ 5. Naive Bayes

Gaussian Naive Bayes baseline with default and adjusted variance smoothing (var_smoothing) to stabilize probability estimates.

from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB nb_variants = { "Naive Bayes (default)": GaussianNB(), "Naive Bayes (var_smoothing=1e-6)": GaussianNB(var_smoothing=1e-6), } nb_cms = {} for name, model in nb_variants.items(): metrics, cm = evaluate_model(name, model, X_train_s, y_train, X_test_s, y_test) nb_cms[name] = cm print(name, "->", metrics)

⌄ 6. Support Vector Machine (SVM)

Comparing linear hyper-planes against non-linear Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels with varying penalty parameters (C=1.0 vs C=10.0).

from sklearn.svm import SVC svm_variants = { "SVM (linear, C=1)": SVC(kernel="linear", C=1, probability=True, random_state=42), "SVM (rbf, C=1)": SVC(kernel="rbf", C=1, probability=True, random_state=42), "SVM (rbf, C=10, gamma='scale')": SVC(kernel="rbf", C=10, gamma="scale", probability=True, random_state=42), } svm_cms = {} for name, model in svm_variants.items(): metrics, cm = evaluate_model(name, model, X_train_s, y_train, X_test_s, y_test) svm_cms[name] = cm print(name, "->", metrics)
SVM (linear, C=1) -> {'Model': 'SVM (linear, C=1)', 'Accuracy': 0.8537, 'Precision': 0.8696, 'Recall': 0.8537, 'F1': 0.8404, 'Train time (s)': 0.036, 'Log Loss': 0.4152, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7644} SVM (rbf, C=1) -> {'Model': 'SVM (rbf, C=1)', 'Accuracy': 0.8537, 'Precision': 0.8696, 'Recall': 0.8537, 'F1': 0.8404, 'Train time (s)': 0.0868, 'Log Loss': 0.4145, 'ROC-AUC': 0.8303} SVM (rbf, C=10, gamma='scale') -> {'Model': 'SVM (rbf, C=10, gamma='scale')', 'Accuracy': 0.8537, 'Precision': 0.8540, 'Recall': 0.8537, 'F1': 0.8466, 'Train time (s)': 0.1721, 'Log Loss': 0.4686, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7923}
⌄ 7. Decision Tree — CART

CART binary decision trees utilizing Gini Impurity and Information Gain (Entropy) splits across varying maximum tree depths.

from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier, plot_tree dt_variants = { "Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=None)": DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion="gini", random_state=42), "Decision Tree (entropy, max_depth=5)": DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion="entropy", max_depth=5, random_state=42), "Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=3)": DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion="gini", max_depth=3, random_state=42), } dt_cms = {} for name, model in dt_variants.items(): metrics, cm = evaluate_model(name, model, X_train_s, y_train, X_test_s, y_test) dt_cms[name] = cm print(name, "->", metrics)
Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=None) -> {'Model': 'Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=None)', 'Accuracy': 0.7561, 'Precision': 0.7561, 'Recall': 0.7561, 'F1': 0.7561, 'Train time (s)': 0.0101, 'Log Loss': 8.7911, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7144} Decision Tree (entropy, max_depth=5) -> {'Model': 'Decision Tree (entropy, max_depth=5)', 'Accuracy': 0.8211, 'Precision': 0.8195, 'Recall': 0.8211, 'F1': 0.8103, 'Train time (s)': 0.0056, 'Log Loss': 1.3237, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7519} Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=3) -> {'Model': 'Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=3)', 'Accuracy': 0.8455, 'Precision': 0.8633, 'Recall': 0.8455, 'F1': 0.8303, 'Train time (s)': 0.0023, 'Log Loss': 0.9868, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7375}
# Visualize the shallow tree (max_depth=3) plt.figure(figsize=(15, 7.5)) plot_tree(trained_models["Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=3)"], filled=True, fontsize=8) plt.title("Decision Tree (gini, max_depth=3)") plt.show()
⌄ 8. Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)

Testing single-layer and multi-layer neural architectures with backpropagation, observing gradient convergence via training loss curves.

from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier mlp_variants = { "MLP (32,) relu": MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(32,), activation="relu", max_iter=500, random_state=42), "MLP (64,32) relu": MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(64, 32), activation="relu", max_iter=500, random_state=42), "MLP (64,32) tanh, lr=0.01": MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(64, 32), activation="tanh", learning_rate_init=0.01, max_iter=500, random_state=42), } mlp_cms = {} for name, model in mlp_variants.items(): metrics, cm = evaluate_model(name, model, X_train_s, y_train, X_test_s, y_test) mlp_cms[name] = cm print(name, "->", metrics)
MLP (32,) relu -> {'Model': 'MLP (32,) relu', 'Accuracy': 0.8130, 'Precision': 0.8076, 'Recall': 0.8130, 'F1': 0.8072, 'Train time (s)': 0.9955, 'Log Loss': 0.4571, 'ROC-AUC': 0.8241} MLP (64,32) relu -> {'Model': 'MLP (64,32) relu', 'Accuracy': 0.7642, 'Precision': 0.7552, 'Recall': 0.7642, 'F1': 0.7569, 'Train time (s)': 1.8335, 'Log Loss': 1.1100, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7774} MLP (64,32) tanh, lr=0.01 -> {'Model': 'MLP (64,32) tanh, lr=0.01', 'Accuracy': 0.7480, 'Precision': 0.7429, 'Recall': 0.7480, 'F1': 0.7450, 'Train time (s)': 1.2135, 'Log Loss': 1.1039, 'ROC-AUC': 0.7731}
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4.5)) for name in ["MLP (32,) relu", "MLP (64,32) relu", "MLP (64,32) tanh, lr=0.01"]: plt.plot(trained_models[name].loss_curve_, label=name) plt.xlabel("Iteration") plt.ylabel("Training Loss") plt.title("MLP Training Loss Curves") plt.legend() plt.show()
